In [[mathematical logic]], the '''Friedman translation''' is a certain transformation of [[well-formed formula|formula]]s. Among other things it can be used to show that the [[arithmetical hierarchy|Π<sup>0</sup><sub style="margin-left:-0.65em">2</sub>]]-theorems of various [[first-order theories]] of [[classical logic|classical mathematics]] are also theorems of [[intuitionistic logic|intuitionistic]] mathematics. It is named after its discoverer, [[Harvey Friedman (mathematician)|Harvey Friedman]].

==Definition==
Let ''A'' and ''B'' be formulas, where no [[free variable]] of ''B'' is [[bound variable|quantified]] in ''A''. The translation ''A<sup>B</sup>'' is defined by replacing each [[atomic formula|atomic]] [[subformula]] ''C'' of ''A'' by {{nowrap|''C'' ∨ ''B''}}. For purposes of the translation, ⊥ is considered to be an atomic formula as well; hence it is replaced with {{nowrap|⊥ ∨ ''B''}} (which is equivalent to ''B''). The translation is relevant in an intuitionistic context and here ¬''A'' is generally defined as an abbreviation for {{nowrap|''A'' → ⊥;}} hence {{nowrap|(¬''A'')<sup>''B''</sup> {{=}} ''A<sup>B</sup>'' → ''B''.}}

==Application==
The Friedman translation can be used to show the closure of many intuitionistic theories under the [[Markov rule]], and to obtain [[conservative extension|partial conservativity]] results.  The key condition is that the <math>\Delta^0_0</math>-sentences of the logic be [[Decidability (logic)|decidable]], allowing the unquantified theorems of the intuitionistic and classical theories to coincide.

For example, if ''A'' is provable in [[Heyting arithmetic]] (HA), then ''A<sup>B</sup>'' is also provable in HA.<ref>Harvey Friedman. Classically and Intuitionistically Provably Recursive Functions. In Scott, D. S. and Muller, G. H. Editors, Higher Set Theory, Volume 699 of Lecture Notes in Mathematics, Springer Verlag (1978), pp. 21–28. {{doi|10.1007/BFb0103100}}</ref> Moreover, if ''A'' is a [[arithmetical hierarchy|Σ<sup>0</sup><sub style="margin-left:-0.65em">1</sub>-formula]], then ''A<sup>B</sup>'' is in HA equivalent to {{nowrap|''A'' ∨ ''B''}}. By setting ''B'' = ''A'', this implies that:
*Heyting arithmetic is closed under the primitive recursive Markov rule (MP<sub>PR</sub>): if the formula ¬¬''A'' is provable in HA, where ''A'' is a Σ<sup>0</sup><sub style="margin-left:-0.65em">1</sub>-formula, then ''A'' is also provable in HA.
*[[Peano arithmetic]] is Π<sup>0</sup><sub style="margin-left:-0.65em">2</sub>-conservative over Heyting arithmetic: if Peano arithmetic proves a Π<sup>0</sup><sub style="margin-left:-0.65em">2</sub>-formula ''A'', then ''A'' is already provable in HA.
